title: Playing a Chris Kelly record and discussing his solos
summary: A record of Careless Love is played; Howard describes Chris's wah-wah solos and bands with featured soloists.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Let me put on a record now, since you're talking about Chris. I'm going to play this, Callous Love, that came out first on the climax.
Yeah.
Can you hear it?
Yeah, I can hear it. That's the way he was starting. These men on the record.

I know they shouldn't. I guess most of the fellas in that band played with Chris at one time, aren't you? Yeah, George. That's right. I know they should. I guess most of the fellas in that band played with Chris at one time or another. Yeah, George. That's right.
Big Jim. I know they should.
I guess most of the fellas in that band played with Chris at one time or another. Yeah, George.
That's right. Big Jim.
Yeah. That's right.
Big Jim.
Would he play it like this, this boy? That's just the way he used to play. That's what the other fellows tell me too. That's right.
Oh, long years ago I used to play exactly like it.
Would he have a solo with his band?
Oh yeah, with the wah-wah. He'd take the wah-wah, most of his solos would be with that.
Would he let the clarinet play a solo like that?
Oh yeah, oh yeah.
Do you remember any bands that didn't have solos, that had ensemble all the time?
Well most all the bands that I know in my time, this man would stand out for himself.
Yeah. Would he do that little lick you just played, Chris? No, he didn't play like that.
And he'd play that solo like that. But he'd have that wah-wah with that little mute in it. Take that. Take that. Mm-hm. I'm still out of tape.
